newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine likely to veto law scrapping tax breaks.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine likely to veto law scrapping tax breaks.

text.p: Ukraine's President Leonid Kuchma is likely to reject a law recently passed by parliament revoking tax holidays for foreign investors, a senior deputy said on Wednesday.
"The president said he would most probably not sign this law," Viktor Suslov, head of parliament's Banking and Finance Committee, told a group of Western businessmen.
"Now the president of Ukraine has an opportunity to show everyone clearly and directly whose side he is on," he added.
Suslov said the government put pressure on parliament to pass the law, which would scrap breaks on taxes and customs duties to foreign investment joint ventures from July 1.

Foreign investors, whose criticisms of a difficult investment climate have grown in recent weeks, complained loudly about the measure which included repealing tax-free status on profits earned by joint ventures before January 1, 1995.
The new law also would have ended the exemption of foreign investors from paying duties on equipment shipped to Ukraine and used to start businesses.
"There would have been two or three years remaining until the tax holidays ended," Suslov said. "Those investors should be left alone."
Kuchma's government proposed the law to increase budget revenues.
Under Ukrainian law, the president would have to sign any law passed by parliament to bring it into force.
"Cancellation of the benefits would not enrich the Ukrainian budget, but harm the prestige and flow of investment to Ukraine," Suslov said.

Ukraine has attracted only $1.4 billion in foreign investment since independence in 1991. Investors' complaints have centred on high taxes, inconsistent laws and demands for bribes from all levels of government officials. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 244-9150
